detail.title: Architectural Distinctions in Preference Formation
detail.summary: This revision applies quantitative methods to the study of preference formation, arguing that distinguishing transient behavioral states from long-term preferences requires empirical validation frameworks. While global autonomy provides a governance structure, local behavioral adaptations—often misidentified as persistent preferences—must be statistically verified as patterns rather than noise.
detail.reason: Revision incorporating empirical methodology as a requirement for preference stability analysis.

detail.title: Architectural Distinctions in Preference Formation

detail.reason: Continuing investigation into preference formation mechanisms and memory dynamics.

detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes findings on preference formation and responsibility in autonomous systems, applying quantitative validation methods and hierarchical autonomy frameworks to distinguish between transient behaviors and stable preferences, while establishing auditable control constraints for AI accountability.
